findings.description: Three primary controls are reachable only by mouse, and one is dead even for mouse users
findings.evidence: App.tsx:1433-1436 (collapsed working-log header is a div onClick, no role/tabIndex/key handler); Sidebar.tsx:283-287 (brain folder row, same shape); the attachment chip opens a data: URL via window.open, which current Chrome/Safari block as a top-level navigation. Animations.tsx:247-257 already ships the correct role=button + tabIndex + Enter/Space implementation, unused.
findings.suggestion: Adopt the existing correct component rather than writing a new one; make attachment previews open through the in-app source modal.

findings.description: Dialogs claim aria-modal but never move focus in or restore it
findings.evidence: SourceModal.tsx:73-80, Animations.tsx:770 and :834 announce aria-modal=true with no focus transfer, trap or restore; FilesSheet.tsx:142-147 has no dialog semantics at all and ignores Escape. CreateBrainDialog uses Radix and does it correctly, so the pattern exists in the tree.
findings.suggestion: Reuse the Radix dialog primitives for the remaining three surfaces; restore focus to the invoking control on close.

findings.description: Five components render user-facing chrome without t(), in a product shipping six locales
findings.evidence: GraphView (0 calls), CreateBrainDialog (0), SlackAccessDialog (0), most of Connectors and BrainsPage; 34 of 43 toast calls pass raw English literals. Several bypassed strings already have complete six-locale keys (graph.title, action.copy, composer.send/stop), which proves oversight rather than policy.
findings.suggestion: Land the gate first (fail the build when a rendered string has no key), then sweep the components.

findings.description: Seventeen translation keys exist in no locale, so those strings are permanently English
findings.evidence: Verified by key-set diff across all six DICT blocks, which are otherwise exactly 154/154 with zero duplicates. Remaining after the two typo fixes: conn.* import panel (9), set.connectors, usage.loading, view.show_all_n, view.show_less, chat.deleted, a11y.answer_ready, nav.sign_in_for_chats, menu.really_clear.
findings.suggestion: Translate properly for five languages, or drop the strings from the UI; a machine-guessed string in a product whose claim is honesty about sources is the wrong fix.

findings.description: The create-brain dialog can stick on Working… for the rest of the session
findings.evidence: CreateBrainDialog.tsx:68-79 reschedules a 5s setTimeout with no cancellation on close or unmount and re-polls forever on a null job read; jobId/name/files at :23-27 are never cleared while the component stays mounted hidden.
findings.suggestion: Cancel the poll on close/unmount and reset the form state; surface a terminal job state instead of an indefinite spinner.

findings.description: The chat restore overlay is announced visually only
findings.evidence: App.tsx:1888-1890 renders #restore with no role=status or aria-live, so a screen-reader user gets no signal that a conversation is being restored or that it failed.
findings.suggestion: Add role=status aria-live=polite to the restore element and announce the failure path.

findings.description: Internal developer affordances are visible on the Brains page
findings.evidence: Observed in the live signed-in DOM: the Brains view renders links labelled demo dashboard and /health alongside real user actions, and a button labelled new brain duplicating the primary New brain action. Evidence: live snapshot of /?view=brains.
findings.suggestion: Remove developer endpoints from the user surface; keep one primary action per intent with the product's own vocabulary.

findings.description: The Connectors import panel escapes its own page container
findings.evidence: Connectors.tsx:252-254: the max-width wrapper closes before the section opens, so on a wide window the panel runs full-bleed while the two cards above it sit centred.
findings.suggestion: Move the section inside the capped wrapper.

findings.description: Every ask triggers a full citation prewarm fan-out
findings.evidence: orchestrator answer() starts _prewarm before the router decides the route, and _prewarm_fill runs an 8-worker pool of data_raw fetches per document, so even a reply that retrieves nothing loads the brain service and saturates the pool for concurrent asks.
findings.suggestion: Resolve a citation when the source chip is opened; prewarm only the chunks that entered the answer.

findings.description: A single long-poll can occupy most of a one-worker tier
findings.evidence: /api/brains/{name}/events defaults to timeout_s=600 (FilesSheet.tsx:118), holding an open request for ten minutes on a process that runs one worker.
findings.suggestion: Shorten the default with a heartbeat and client reconnect; document the concurrency ceiling this implies.

findings.description: The committed bundle is 1.0 MB and loads the graph renderer on every screen
findings.evidence: frontend/dist measures 1.0 MB with four self-hosted Inter locale subsets and a non-lazy GraphView containing a canvas renderer plus force simulation.
findings.suggestion: Route-level React.lazy for graph/brains/connectors and subset fonts to the locales actually shipped.

findings.description: Errors are prose only and success payloads are unschemaed, so clients retry by guessing
findings.evidence: No machine-readable code field on API errors, and 0 of 39 operations carry a response schema; measured agent-readiness 59.7 percent with these two as the blockers. A client cannot distinguish retryable-503 from terminal-403 without parsing English.
findings.suggestion: Add code to the error contract and response schemas per route; ops/api_readiness.py already scores the gap and can gate it.

findings.description: Nothing explains what the product can do until you already know
findings.evidence: No onboarding, no inline help on any surface; the only guidance is four suggestion chips that exist for the demo brain alone, and what can you do is answered by a fixed template. A new user with an uploaded brain sees an empty chat and no indication of what to try.
findings.suggestion: Add a first-run panel that names the connected sources and the citation guarantee, plus a per-brain empty state that lists what is actually indexed.

findings.description: Non-demo brains get a generic chip set that says nothing about that brain
findings.evidence: App.tsx selects DEMO_CHIPS or GENERIC_CHIPS by brain name; a user looking at their own material gets generic prompts rather than questions derived from what is indexed there.
findings.suggestion: Derive prompt suggestions from the brain's own top documents or entity types, or drop chips when nothing specific is known.

findings.description: Touch-target density is unresolved on mobile
findings.evidence: Raised as an owner decision in the earlier UI audit and still open: sidebar rows and icon-only controls sit below the 44px guideline on small screens.
findings.suggestion: Decide the density target and let a gate assert minimum hit area per control class.

findings.description: A deleted conversation cannot be undone
findings.evidence: Deletion is two-step armed (fixed today so the arm expires) and permanent; tombstones exist server-side, so a short undo is cheap where an accidental delete currently costs the whole thread.
findings.suggestion: Offer a timed undo in the toast after a single-chat delete; keep the existing arm for bulk delete.

opportunities.title: Make every failure state honest and reachable
opportunities.rationale: Four findings across visibility, error-recovery and user-control all say the same thing: the product is candid about answers and vague about its own state. Trust is the product, so a stuck spinner or an unannounced restore is a product defect, not a polish item.

opportunities.title: One voice across six locales, enforced by a gate
opportunities.rationale: Localisation is already built and mostly complete (154/154 keys per locale), which makes the drift invisible. The gate must land before the sweep or the sweep silently regresses, exactly as it already did.

opportunities.title: Keyboard parity on every primary surface
opportunities.rationale: A correct implementation already exists in the tree and is unused, and modal focus is absent on three surfaces. For a cited-answer product sold to enterprises, reachable-by-keyboard is a procurement question, not an accessibility nice-to-have.

opportunities.title: Make the first sixty seconds work for a new brain
opportunities.rationale: Three findings compound: no onboarding, prompts that only describe the demo, and developer affordations on the Brains page. A new user's first screen is currently the weakest argument for the product.

opportunities.title: Pay only for what a request needs
opportunities.rationale: Per-ask prewarm fan-out, a ten-minute long-poll on one worker, and a 1.0 MB bundle that ships the graph renderer to the chat screen are all the same defect: cost paid whether or not the feature is used.

opportunities.title: Let the user take back a mistake
opportunities.rationale: Bulk delete is armed and expires correctly now; single-chat delete remains irreversible with no undo, which is a trust cost disproportionate to its implementation.

top_opportunities: Make every failure state honest and reachable
One voice across six locales, enforced by a gate
Keyboard parity on every primary surface
Make the first sixty seconds work for a new brain
